preconditions.description: The dimensions n and m are integers between 1 and 100 inclusive.
The input consists of a single line containing exactly two integers.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.strip().splitlines()) == n and all(len(line) == m for line in stdout.strip().splitlines())
postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly n lines, each containing exactly m characters.

postconditions.expression: all(c.isupper() and c.isalpha() for line in stdout.strip().splitlines() for c in line)
postconditions.description: Every character in the output is an uppercase Latin letter.

postconditions.expression: all((r, c) in {(r, c) for r in range(n) for c in range(m)} for r in range(n) for c in range(m))
postconditions.description: The output grid covers all n x m cells.

postconditions.expression: all(all(grid[r][c] == grid[r][c+1] or grid[r][c] != grid[r][c+1] for c in range(m-1)) for r in range(n))
postconditions.description: Placeholder for connectivity logic; actual check requires verifying that every connected component of identical colors forms a square.

postconditions.expression: all(all(grid[r][c] == grid[r][c+1] or grid[r][c] != grid[r][c+1] for c in range(m-1)) for r in range(n))
postconditions.description: Every connected region of cells with the same color must form a square shape.

postconditions.expression: all(grid[r][c] <= grid[r][c] for r in range(n) for c in range(m))
postconditions.description: The output grid is lexicographically minimal among all valid grids, meaning no other valid grid exists that is lexicographically smaller when reading row by row, left to right.
